title: IdentityProviderConnection

$schema.description: Editor affordance: path or URL of this schema so editors validate and autocomplete the file (scaffolded connection files point at `.zitadel/meta/idp-connection.json`). Ignored by the platform.

slug.description: Stable identifier, referenced by user schemas (`x-auth-methods.sso.providers`) and flow steps (`sso_providers`). Unique within the project.

protocol.description: The protocol used by the identity provider. OIDC is the only protocol.

template.description: Template hint for rendering the provider (logo, colors). It carries no protocol behavior: that comes only from the protocol blocks.

display_name.description: Shown to the user on the sign-in button.

subject_claim.description: Claim carrying the provider's stable subject identifier. Optional. When omitted, `sub` is used, as the OIDC specification says. Override it where `sub` is pairwise, for example Entra `oid`.

claim_mapping.description: Maps user-schema property names (keys) to provider claim names (values). A value is an exact top-level claim key. There is no path syntax, and a dot is part of the key, so nested claims (OIDC `address`) are not addressable yet. `$`-prefixed strings and non-string values are reserved for future mapping forms. Add properties defined in the user schemas. Unmatched entries are ignored.

verified_claims.description: Maps a verifiable user-schema property to its verification source: a claim name (read the claim) or the literal `true` (trust this provider unconditionally). Values starting with `$` are reserved for future sources. This differs from `claim_mapping`, which carries values, not verification state.

provisioning.description: How far this provider's data is trusted. `creation` defines what happens to a subject that has no account yet. With `disabled`, no user is created. With `auto`, the user is created without a collection step (a step that asks the user for data) when the mapped claims fill every required property of the schema. A required property with an `x-unique` scope must also arrive verified according to `verified_claims`. When a required property is missing or such a property is unverified, the collection step is shown instead, prefilled with the claims.

oidc.description: OIDC settings of the identity provider. Endpoints come from the issuer's discovery document. A provider that exposes no `.well-known` document names them all instead: `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`, `jwks_uri`, and `userinfo_endpoint` unless `id_token_mapping` is set. Setting any endpoint without the others is rejected with `idp.endpoints_partial`.

issuer.description: Discovery base. Endpoints are resolved from its `.well-known` document unless the connection document names them all.

jwks_uri.description: JWKS endpoint, for a provider that exposes no `.well-known` document. Set together with the other endpoints.

id_token_mapping.description: Reads user claims from the `id_token` instead of the userinfo endpoint, for providers that populate only the former.

authorization_endpoint.description: For a provider that exposes no `.well-known` document. Set together with the other endpoints.

token_endpoint.description: For a provider that exposes no `.well-known` document. Set together with the other endpoints.

userinfo_endpoint.description: For a provider that exposes no `.well-known` document. Set together with the other endpoints. Not needed when `id_token_mapping` is set.

client_id.description: Either a literal, when the same client is used in all environments, or a `${{ NAME }}` reference to a variable, when each environment has its own client.

client_secret.description: A reference to the variable holding the client secret, never the secret itself. A secret may only be referenced as the entire value: text around the placeholder would be rendered into the resolved credential, so it is rejected. The server resolves it against the environment serving the request.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: How the client authenticates at the token endpoint.

scopes.description: Must contain `openid`: without it the provider returns no id_token, so the identity provider is not OIDC. The `default` only prefills user interfaces. Validators never inject it, so an omitted `scopes` is rejected regardless.

pkce_enabled.description: Sends PKCE (`code_challenge`/`code_verifier`). Providers that do not support PKCE typically ignore the parameters, so `true` is safe. Set `false` only for a provider whose token endpoint rejects them.

static_authorize_parameters.description: Extra provider-specific authorize parameters (for example `prompt`). Protocol parameters that the server sets itself are reserved and rejected: an override of `state` or `nonce` would silently defeat CSRF and token binding. `client_secret` and `client_assertion` are rejected because they could be appended to the public authorize URL.
